scores.evidence: The flowchart TD screen-flow diagram (s2-b4) shows its labels clearly at 390 px and has a caption and a 図の説明を読む / 'Describe the figure in words' text alternative (pages/mobile-jp-14.png). The two-column tables s2-table and the MoSCoW table in s5-b2 wrap without clipping on mobile (pages/mobile-jp-07.png, pages/mobile-jp-09.png).

textOnlyScreens is empty on every viewport. Each screen has a heading, a definition box, a table, steps, a prompt or a check, and paragraphs stay at 2–4 lines on desktop. Desktop JP median is 37 chars per line (target 30–40) and EN median is 73 (target 60–75).

The EN screens have no leftover Japanese, including the diagram labels ('Money-left screen', 'Add button'), the prompt placeholders ('app idea', 'app name') and the flashcards. The JP screens use Japanese diagram labels, and no control is hidden under the 56/60 px mobile bars.

niceToHave: Desktop JP charsPerLine max is 42, a little over the 40 target, while the median of 37 is fine. In s2-defs the 機能 definition leaves 「す。」 alone on the last line on desktop (pages/desktop-jp-04.png). Shortening it to 「…アプリが『すること』。」 would avoid that one-character widow.
reader: on mobile the flashcard hint says 「クリックまたはスペースキーでめくる」 (pages/mobile-jp-23.png). Touch devices should get 「タップでめくる」 instead.

reader: the check section shows 理解度チェック twice, once as the section heading and again as the card label right below it (pages/desktop-jp-11.png, pages/mobile-jp-16.png). The card label could be dropped when it repeats the section title.
summary: No hard failures: no horizontal overflow, console, mermaid, unknown-block or broken-image errors. The tables, the TD diagram and the prompt blocks are easy to read at 390 px and fully localized in EN. The only visual nit in the lesson content is a one-character widow in the s2-defs definition; the other notes are about the reader.
